text: SOURCE: WHO & Ministry of Health — Cardiovascular Emergency Guidelines CATEGORY: Cardiac, Emergency, Chest Pain TAGS: chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, rapid heartbeat, sweating, dizziness, fainting --- HEART ATTACK (MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION) --- A heart attack occurs when blood flow to the heart is blocked, causing heart muscle damage. This is a life-threatening emergency. Warning Signs of Heart Attack: - Chest pain or pressure (often described as squeezing, tightness, or crushing) - Pain radiating to left arm, shoulder, neck, jaw, or back - Shortness of breath - Cold sweats - Nausea and vomiting - Lightheadedness or dizziness - Sudden fatigue - Palpitations ⚠️ EMERGENCY: Call 112 (India) or go to nearest emergency room immediately. Note: Women may present atypically — more nausea, back pain, jaw pain, fatigue without chest pain. First Aid: - Call emergency services immediately - Chew aspirin 300mg (if not allergic and not contraindicated) - Keep patient calm and still - Loosen tight clothing - Begin CPR if unconscious and not breathing --- ANGINA PECTORIS --- Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart, usually triggered by exertion. Symptoms: - Chest pain, pressure, or tightness - Usually triggered by physical activity or stress - Relieved by rest (stable angina) or occurs at rest (unstable angina) - May radiate to arm, jaw, or shoulder - Shortness of breath Treatment: - Sublingual nitroglycerine for acute episodes (prescribed) - Beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers (chronic management) - Lifestyle: quit smoking, reduce cholesterol, control blood pressure Unstable angina = Emergency — seek care immediately. --- HYPERTENSIVE URGENCY / EMERGENCY --- Severely elevated blood pressure (> 180/120 mmHg). Symptoms: - Severe headache - Shortness of breath - Chest pain - Nausea/vomiting - Vision changes - Confusion or altered consciousness ⚠️ Seek emergency care immediately. --- CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS --- Irregular heart rhythms

— seek care immediately. --- HYPERTENSIVE URGENCY / EMERGENCY --- Severely elevated blood pressure (> 180/120 mmHg). Symptoms: - Severe headache - Shortness of breath - Chest pain - Nausea/vomiting - Vision changes - Confusion or altered consciousness ⚠️ Seek emergency care immediately. --- CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS --- Irregular heart rhythms that can cause symptoms. Symptoms: - Palpitations (fluttering, racing heart) - Dizziness - Shortness of breath - Chest discomfort - Fainting or near-fainting Common types: - Atrial fibrillation (irregular, rapid) - Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) - Bradycardia (slow heart rate) Treatment depends on type — requires ECG diagnosis and medical management. --- PULMONARY EMBOLISM --- Blood clot in the lungs. Symptoms: - Sudden shortness of breath - Chest pain (sharp, worsens with breathing) - Rapid heart rate - Coughing up blood - Leg pain/swelling (if DVT present) - Dizziness or fainting ⚠️ EMERGENCY — Call 112 immediately. Risk factors: Prolonged immobility, surgery, obesity, prior clots, oral contraceptives Treatment: Anticoagulants (heparin, warfarin), thrombolytics in severe cases

SOURCE: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India — Dengue Fever Guidelines CATEGORY: Dengue, Vector-Borne Disease TAGS: fever, headache, joint pain, body pain, rash, nausea, vomiting, fatigue --- DENGUE FEVER --- Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti. Dengue is endemic in India and prevalent during and after monsoon season. Symptoms of Dengue (Classic): - Sudden high fever (39–40°C) lasting 2–7 days - Severe headache (especially behind the eyes — retro-orbital pain) - Joint pain and muscle pain (dengue is called "breakbone fever") - Body aches - Skin rash (appears 2–5 days after fever onset — flat red rash) - Nausea and vomiting - Fatigue Warning Signs of Severe Dengue (Seek Emergency Care Immediately): - Abdominal pain or tenderness - Persistent vomiting (3 or more times in 24 hours) - Bleeding from gums, nose, or in vomit/stool - Rapid breathing - Fatigue and restlessness - Blood in urine, stool, or vomit - Platelet count falling rapidly Diagnosis: - NS1 antigen test (positive in first 5 days) - Dengue IgM/IgG antibody test (after 5 days) - Complete Blood Count (CBC) — platelet and WBC count Treatment (No specific antiviral): - Strict bed rest - Oral rehydration — drink at least 2–3 liters of water/ORS daily - Paracetamol for fever (500–1000mg every 6 hours for adults) - AVOID: Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Diclofenac (increase bleeding risk) - Monitor platelet count daily from day 3 of fever - Hospitalization if platelet < 50,000/mm³ or warning signs present Prevention: - Eliminate mosquito breeding sites (stagnant water) - Use mosquito repellents and nets - Wear long-sleeved clothing - Community fogging programs Key Differentiating Features from Flu: - Retro-orbital eye pain - Rash appearance after 2–4 days - Thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) - More severe joint/muscle

SOURCE: World Health Organization (WHO) — Influenza and Fever Guidelines CATEGORY: Fever, Influenza, Respiratory Infections TAGS: fever, headache, body pain, fatigue, chills, cough, sore throat --- FEVER --- Fever is defined as a body temperature above 38°C (100.4°F). It is a common sign of infection and the immune system's response to pathogens. Common Causes of Fever: - Viral infections: influenza, common cold, dengue, COVID-19 - Bacterial infections: typhoid, urinary tract infection, pneumonia - Other: heat exhaustion, autoimmune conditions, drug reactions Symptoms typically associated with fever: - Body temperature above 38°C - Chills and shivering - Sweating - Headache - Muscle pain and body aches - Fatigue and weakness - Loss of appetite Management of Fever: - Rest and hydration (oral rehydration salts if needed) - Paracetamol (acetaminophen): 500–1000mg every 4–6 hours for adults (do not exceed 4g/day) - Ibuprofen (if no contraindications): 400mg every 8 hours - Tepid sponging for comfort - Monitor temperature every 4 hours Seek emergency care if: - Temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F) - Fever in infants under 3 months (any fever = emergency) - Fever persists beyond 3 days - Associated with stiff neck, rash, confusion, or difficulty breathing - Febrile seizure occurs --- INFLUENZA (FLU) --- Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. It spreads via respiratory droplets. Symptoms of Influenza: - Sudden onset high fever (38–40°C) - Severe headache - Muscle aches and body pain - Extreme fatigue - Dry cough - Sore throat - Runny or stuffy nose - Chills Duration: 5–7 days for most symptoms; fatigue may last 2 weeks. Treatment: - Bed rest - Adequate hydration - Antipyretics for fever (paracetamol preferred) - Antiviral medications (oseltamivir/Tamiflu) within 48 hours for high-risk groups - Isolation to prevent spread Prevention: - Annual influenza vaccination (recommended by WHO) - Hand hygiene

SOURCE: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) — Gastrointestinal Disease Guidelines CATEGORY: Gastrointestinal, Diarrhea, Food Poisoning, Gastroenteritis TAGS: diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, stomach ache, loss of appetite, bloating --- ACUTE GASTROENTERITIS --- Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically caused by viral (norovirus, rotavirus) or bacterial infection. Symptoms: - Nausea and vomiting - Diarrhea (watery or loose stools) - Abdominal cramps and pain - Low-grade fever - Fatigue - Loss of appetite - Headache Duration: 1–3 days (viral), up to 5–7 days (bacterial) Treatment: - Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS): Gold standard. WHO-recommended ORS composition: 2.6g NaCl, 2.9g sodium citrate, 1.5g KCl, 13.5g glucose per liter of water. - Drink small sips frequently to prevent vomiting - BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast - Zinc supplementation for children (20mg/day for 10 days) - Probiotics (Lactobacillus) may reduce duration - Antibiotics only if bacterial infection confirmed (azithromycin, ciprofloxacin) Danger Signs — Seek Medical Attention: - Blood or mucus in stool - High fever (> 39°C) - Signs of dehydration: dry mouth, no urination, sunken eyes, dizziness - Persistent vomiting preventing oral rehydration - Diarrhea lasting more than 3 days --- FOOD POISONING --- Caused by consuming contaminated food with bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli, Staphylococcus) or their toxins. Symptoms (onset: 1–72 hours after contaminated food): - Sudden nausea - Vomiting - Diarrhea (may be bloody) - Abdominal cramps - Fever - Weakness High-risk foods in India: - Undercooked meat and poultry - Raw or improperly handled dairy - Leftover rice (Bacillus cereus) - Street food with poor hygiene Treatment: Similar to gastroenteritis (ORS, rest, BRAT diet) --- IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME (IBS) --- IBS is a chronic functional disorder affecting the large intestine. Symptoms: - Abdominal pain or cramping (often relieved after bowel movement) - Bloating - Alternating constipation and diarrhea

(Bacillus cereus) - Street food with poor hygiene Treatment: Similar to gastroenteritis (ORS, rest, BRAT diet) --- IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME (IBS) --- IBS is a chronic functional disorder affecting the large intestine. Symptoms: - Abdominal pain or cramping (often relieved after bowel movement) - Bloating - Alternating constipation and diarrhea - Mucus in stool - Gas Management: - High-fiber diet - Avoid trigger foods (dairy, fatty foods, alcohol, caffeine) - Stress management - Antispasmodics (mebeverine) for cramps - Loperamide for diarrhea-predominant IBS - Fiber supplements (ispaghula husk) for constipation-predominant IBS --- PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE --- Sores in the lining of the stomach or upper small intestine. Symptoms: - Burning stomach pain (often between meals) - Nausea - Bloating - Heartburn - Loss of appetite - Dark or bloody stools (severe) Causes: H. pylori infection, NSAIDs, stress Treatment: - Proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole, pantoprazole) - H. pylori eradication therapy if confirmed (triple therapy: PPI + 2 antibiotics) - Avoid NSAIDs, alcohol, smoking

SOURCE: WHO & ICMR — Musculoskeletal and Neurological Conditions CATEGORY: Musculoskeletal, Neurological TAGS: joint pain, back pain, muscle pain, body pain, headache, dizziness, weakness, numbness --- MALARIA --- Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through Anopheles mosquito bites. Endemic in India. Symptoms: - Cyclical fever with chills (every 48–72 hours depending on type) - Severe headache - Muscle and joint pain - Nausea and vomiting - Fatigue - Sweating after fever breaks - Anemia (in chronic cases) Types prevalent in India: - P. vivax (most common, less severe) - P. falciparum (severe, potentially fatal) Diagnosis: Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT), peripheral blood smear, PCR Treatment: - P. vivax: Chloroquine + Primaquine - P. falciparum: Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT) — artemether-lumefantrine ⚠️ Severe malaria = Emergency. Signs: altered consciousness, respiratory distress, severe anemia, renal failure. Prevention: Insecticide-treated bed nets, indoor spraying, antimalarial prophylaxis for high-risk areas. --- TYPHOID FEVER --- Caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food and water. Symptoms: - Prolonged fever (stepwise rise over 1 week, reaching 39–40°C) - Severe headache - Abdominal pain and distension - Loss of appetite - Constipation (early) then diarrhea - Rose spots on trunk (faint pink macules) - Weakness and fatigue - Relative bradycardia (slow pulse despite high fever) Diagnosis: Blood culture (gold standard), Widal test, Typhidot Treatment: - Ceftriaxone (IV) or azithromycin (oral) — for sensitive strains - Fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin) — where sensitivity confirmed --- ARTHRITIS / JOINT PAIN --- Joint pain can be caused by many conditions. Rheumatoid Arthritis: - Symmetric joint involvement (both sides) - Morning stiffness > 1 hour - Swelling, warmth, tenderness in joints - Small joints first (fingers, wrists) - Fatigue, fever Osteoarthritis: - Joint pain with activity, relieved by rest - Affects weight-bearing joints (knees, hips) - Morning stiffness < 30 minutes

Rheumatoid Arthritis: - Symmetric joint involvement (both sides) - Morning stiffness > 1 hour - Swelling, warmth, tenderness in joints - Small joints first (fingers, wrists) - Fatigue, fever Osteoarthritis: - Joint pain with activity, relieved by rest - Affects weight-bearing joints (knees, hips) - Morning stiffness < 30 minutes - No systemic inflammation Management: - NSAIDs (ibuprofen) for pain relief - Disease-modifying drugs (methotrexate) for RA - Physiotherapy and exercise - Weight management --- MIGRAINE --- A primary headache disorder with moderate-to-severe throbbing pain. Symptoms: - Throbbing, pulsating headache (often unilateral) - Nausea and vomiting - Sensitivity to light (photophobia) and sound (phonophobia) - Aura: visual disturbances, tingling (in some patients) - Duration: 4–72 hours Triggers: Stress, sleep changes, hormonal changes, certain foods (cheese, wine, chocolate), bright lights Acute treatment: - Triptans (sumatriptan) — most effective - NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin) - Antiemetics (metoclopramide) if vomiting Preventive treatment (if > 4 attacks/month): - Beta-blockers (propranolol) - Topiramate - Amitriptyline --- STROKE --- A medical emergency caused by interruption of blood supply to the brain. Recognize Stroke — FAST: - F: Face drooping (uneven smile) - A: Arm weakness (one arm drifts down) - S: Speech difficulty (slurred, confused) - T: Time to call 112 Additional symptoms: - Sudden numbness in face, arm, leg (especially one side) - Sudden confusion - Vision problems - Severe headache with no known cause - Loss of balance or coordination ⚠️ EMERGENCY: Every minute counts. Clot-busting treatment (tPA) must be given within 4.5 hours.

SOURCE: World Health Organization (WHO) — Acute Respiratory Infections CATEGORY: Respiratory, Common Cold, COVID-19, Pneumonia TAGS: cough, sore throat, runny nose, shortness of breath, fever, chest pain, fatigue --- COMMON COLD --- The common cold is a viral upper respiratory tract infection, most often caused by rhinoviruses. Symptoms: - Runny or stuffy nose - Sore throat - Mild cough - Low-grade fever (rare in adults) - Sneezing - Mild headache - Fatigue Duration: 7–10 days Treatment: - Rest and hydration - Saline nasal sprays for congestion - Throat lozenges for sore throat - Paracetamol for fever/pain - Antihistamines for runny nose (first-generation) - No antibiotics required (viral cause) --- ACUTE BRONCHITIS --- Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, usually caused by viral infection. Symptoms: - Persistent cough (can last 2–3 weeks) - Production of mucus (clear, white, yellow, or green) - Shortness of breath - Chest tightness - Wheezing - Mild fever - Fatigue Treatment: - Rest and hydration - Honey and warm water for cough - Cough suppressants for dry, disturbing cough - Bronchodilators if wheezing (consult doctor) - Antibiotics not routinely indicated --- PNEUMONIA --- Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs, which can be bacterial, viral, or fungal. Symptoms: - Productive cough (may contain blood-tinged mucus) - High fever with chills - Shortness of breath - Chest pain (worsens with breathing or coughing) - Rapid breathing - Fatigue and weakness - Confusion (especially in elderly) Seek urgent medical care for pneumonia symptoms. Diagnosis: Chest X-ray, sputum culture, blood tests Treatment: - Antibiotics (bacterial pneumonia — azithromycin, amoxicillin) - Antivirals (viral pneumonia) - Oxygen therapy (if oxygen saturation < 94%) - Hospitalization often required --- COVID-19 --- COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It can range from mild to severe. Common Symptoms: - Fever or chills - Dry

tests Treatment: - Antibiotics (bacterial pneumonia — azithromycin, amoxicillin) - Antivirals (viral pneumonia) - Oxygen therapy (if oxygen saturation < 94%) - Hospitalization often required --- COVID-19 --- COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It can range from mild to severe. Common Symptoms: - Fever or chills - Dry cough - Fatigue - Loss of taste or smell - Headache - Sore throat - Shortness of breath (moderate-severe) - Body aches Emergency Warning Signs (Call emergency services): - Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath - Persistent chest pain - Confusion or inability to wake - Bluish lips or face Prevention: Vaccination, masking, hand hygiene, ventilation --- ASTHMA EXACERBATION --- Asthma is a chronic condition with episodes of airway narrowing. Acute symptoms: - Wheezing - Shortness of breath - Chest tightness - Cough (especially at night) Management: - Short-acting bronchodilator (salbutamol inhaler) for immediate relief - Seek emergency care if no improvement after 2 puffs - Oral corticosteroids for severe exacerbations (prescribed)

SOURCE: ICMR — Dermatological and Allergic Conditions CATEGORY: Skin, Allergy, Dermatology TAGS: skin rash, itching, swelling, jaundice, urticaria, allergic reaction --- URTICARIA (HIVES) --- Urticaria is an itchy skin rash characterized by raised, red welts (wheals). Causes: - Allergic reactions (food, drugs, insect stings) - Infections - Physical triggers (cold, heat, pressure) - Autoimmune conditions Symptoms: - Raised, red, itchy welts on skin - Can appear anywhere on the body - Individual welts typically resolve within 24 hours - May be associated with angioedema (swelling of lips, eyes, throat) ⚠️ Seek emergency care if throat swelling or difficulty breathing (anaphylaxis). Treatment: - Antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine) — first line - Oral corticosteroids (short course) for severe cases - Epinephrine (adrenaline) auto-injector for anaphylaxis --- CONTACT DERMATITIS --- Inflammatory skin reaction from direct contact with an irritant or allergen. Symptoms: - Red rash at contact site - Itching, burning, or stinging - Blisters (in severe cases) - Dry, cracked skin Common triggers: - Metals (nickel), soaps, detergents - Cosmetics, perfumes - Plants (Parthenium, poison ivy) Treatment: - Identify and avoid trigger - Hydrocortisone cream (mild-moderate) - Antihistamines for itching - Moisturizers and emollients --- CHICKENPOX (VARICELLA) --- A highly contagious viral disease caused by Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV). Symptoms: - Fever - Fatigue and malaise - Characteristic rash: starts as red spots → fluid-filled blisters → crusts - Intense itching - Rash progresses from trunk to face and limbs Management: - Calamine lotion for itching - Antihistamines (oral) for itching - Acyclovir (antiviral) for high-risk groups - Keep nails short to prevent scratching - Isolate until all lesions have crusted --- JAUNDICE --- Yellowing of skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels. Symptoms: - Yellow skin and sclera (whites of eyes) - Dark urine (tea-colored) - Pale stools - Fatigue -

(antiviral) for high-risk groups - Keep nails short to prevent scratching - Isolate until all lesions have crusted --- JAUNDICE --- Yellowing of skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels. Symptoms: - Yellow skin and sclera (whites of eyes) - Dark urine (tea-colored) - Pale stools - Fatigue - Itching - Abdominal pain (if liver disease) Causes: - Hepatitis A, B, C - Gallstones - Liver cirrhosis - Hemolytic anemia Diagnosis: Liver function tests (LFT), bilirubin levels, liver ultrasound, hepatitis serology ⚠️ Always seek medical evaluation — jaundice is a sign of underlying disease. --- ANAPHYLAXIS --- A severe, life-threatening allergic reaction. Symptoms (develop within minutes of exposure): - Throat tightening or swelling - Difficulty breathing - Rapid heart rate - Severe skin rash - Vomiting - Dizziness or fainting - Loss of consciousness ⚠️ EMERGENCY: Inject epinephrine (EpiPen) immediately and call 112. Triggers: Food (peanuts, shellfish), bee stings, medications (penicillin), latex
